excerpt: An AdSense readiness checklist based on Google's official eligibility rules and policies: privacy pages, content quality, crawling, and review timing.

edits.find: However, obtaining site authorization has become increasingly rigorous in recent years. Automated compliance bots and human quality review teams routinely reject up to 80% to 90% of initial publisher applications, frequently citing ambiguous policy violations such as "Low Value Content" or "Valueless Inventory."
edits.replace: Google does not publish approval or rejection rates. What it does publish is a short list of AdSense eligibility requirements (original content that meets its policies, access to your site's HTML, and an applicant aged 18 or over) plus the program policies your site is reviewed against. Sites that are not ready typically receive a notice such as "Low value content" or "Site down or unavailable."
edits.reason: Removed unsourced 80-90% rejection statistic; replaced with verified eligibility requirements

edits.find: Whether you are executing a strategy from our guide on How to Start a Tech & Finance Blog (And Make It Profitable Fast) or adapting an existing technical blog for ad monetization, this comprehensive publisher checklist walks you through the exact technical, editorial, and policy standards required to secure AdSense authorization promptly.
edits.replace: Whether you are following our guide on How to Start a Tech & Finance Blog or adapting an existing blog for ad monetization, this checklist walks through the technical, editorial, and policy points to get right before you apply. Following it does not guarantee approval, which is always Google's decision.
edits.reason: Removed "secure authorization promptly" promise; updated stale anchor text

edits.find: Understanding the Two-Stage Google AdSense Review Mechanism
edits.replace: What Google Checks During an AdSense Site Review
edits.reason: Heading claimed an undocumented two-stage mechanism

edits.find: To prepare an application effectively, publishers must first understand how Google evaluates new domains. According to official documentation, the AdSense approval workflow operates through a two-tiered evaluation architecture designed to safeguard advertiser brand safety:
edits.replace: Google does not publicly document the internal stages of its review. Its help pages do say that the review checks your site for policy compliance, that it "usually takes a few days, but in some cases can take 2-4 weeks," and that common blockers include a site that isn't publicly reachable and a robots.txt file that blocks Google's crawler (Google AdSense Help: when your site is not ready to show ads). In practice, the checks fall into two groups:
edits.reason: Replaced claimed "official documentation" of two-tier review with what Google actually documents

edits.find: • Stage 1: Automated Algorithmic Verification: When you place the AdSense verification snippet or connect your property via Google Site Kit, automated crawlers scan your domain. This automated check evaluates server response times, HTTP status codes, SSL encryption, robots.txt directives, structural sitemaps, and basic text-to-code ratios. If your server returns 5xx server errors, exhibits severe latency, or blocks Googlebot, the application is rejected automatically without reaching human reviewers.
edits.replace: • Technical access: After you place the AdSense code or connect your site via Google Site Kit, Google's crawler needs to reach your pages. Server errors, downtime, login walls, firewall rules, or a robots.txt rule that blocks the Mediapartners-Google crawler can stop the review from completing.
edits.reason: Removed invented details of automated check (text-to-code ratio, auto-reject flow)

edits.find: • Stage 2: Human Quality Rater Assessment: Domains that pass the algorithmic verification move to human policy evaluators. These specialists review site legitimacy, user navigation, editorial standards, duplicate content indicators, and adherence to the Google AdSense Program Policies. Human reviewers specifically look for genuine author expertise, transparency, and consumer trust indicators.
edits.replace: • Content and policy compliance: The site is assessed against the Google AdSense Program Policies, including whether it offers enough original, valuable content and a usable navigation. Google does not say which parts of a review are automated and which are manual.
edits.reason: Removed unverified claims about human quality raters

edits.find: A primary reason first-time publishers experience immediate rejection is the absence of required legal and informational documentation. Google requires transparent disclosure regarding data collection, publisher identity, and commercial affiliations. Review teams treat missing legal documents as a failure of basic publishing hygiene.
edits.replace: Google's policies require specific privacy disclosures, and the other pages below are widely recommended because they show readers (and reviewers) who runs the site and how it is funded. Missing basics make a site look unfinished.
edits.reason: Overstated what Google requires; only privacy disclosures are documented as required

edits.find: An AdSense-compliant privacy policy cannot simply be a generic, one-paragraph disclaimer. Google's publisher contract explicitly mandates that you inform visitors regarding third-party vendor tracking, cookie usage, and programmatic personalization. Your privacy policy must disclose:
edits.replace: An AdSense-compliant privacy policy cannot simply be a generic, one-paragraph disclaimer. Google's required content guidance says your privacy policy should cover third-party vendor cookies and how users can opt out. It should disclose:
edits.reason: Added verified source for privacy-policy requirements

edits.find: Google places tremendous emphasis on Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness (E-E-A-T). An anonymous website run by a faceless administrator triggers significant scrutiny during human reviews. Your About Us page should detail:
edits.replace: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness (E-E-A-T) comes from Google Search's helpful-content guidance rather than from the AdSense rules, but clear information about who runs a site helps readers and reviewers alike judge whether it can be trusted. Your About Us page should explain:
edits.reason: E-E-A-T is a Search concept, not an AdSense review criterion; removed unsupported "human review scrutiny" claim

edits.find:
• Individual author profiles, editorial mastheads, or professional qualifications of the contributors.
  • Real physical or registered corporate location, including country and municipal jurisdiction.
edits.replace:
• Who writes the content and their relevant background (do not invent a team or credentials you don't have).
  • Where the site is run from, at least at country level, and business details if you operate as a company.
edits.reason: Softened implied requirements not found in Google policy

edits.find: Generic third-party webmail addresses without additional context may diminish trust scores during manual assessments.
edits.replace: A domain-branded address is not a stated requirement, but it looks more established than a generic webmail address.
edits.reason: Removed invented "trust scores"

edits.find: If your website participates in performance marketing or publishes product roundups, prominent disclosure is legally mandated by consumer protection authorities and Google policies. If you are implementing recommendations from our guide on Affiliate Marketing for Beginners: Step-by-Step Blueprint to Your First $1,000,
edits.replace: If your website earns affiliate commissions or publishes sponsored content, consumer-protection rules such as the U.S. FTC Endorsement Guides require material connections to be disclosed clearly and conspicuously. If you are implementing recommendations from our guide on Affiliate Marketing for Beginners: Complete Step-by-Step Blueprint,
edits.reason: Cited FTC source for disclosure; removed income-promise anchor text

edits.find: The single most common rejection notification received by modern webmasters is "Low Value Content." As outlined in the AdSense Minimum Content Requirements, Google seeks to ensure that advertisers place campaigns alongside unique, high-utility material that commands authentic visitor attention.
edits.replace: "Low value content" is one of the most widely reported rejection notices. Google's AdSense eligibility requirements say your content should be original, high quality, and able to attract an audience.
edits.reason: Unverified "single most common" claim; corrected misnamed link (page is Eligibility requirements)

edits.find: While Google does not publish a rigid numerical post minimum, empirical publishing patterns suggest submitting an application with fewer than 20 to 30 well-researched articles dramatically increases rejection rates. Applying with only 5 or 10 brief articles signals an unestablished property that lacks a sustainable readership baseline.
edits.replace: Google does not publish a minimum number of posts, a word count, or a traffic threshold. Rather than aiming for a number, make sure every section a reviewer might open has substantial, original articles. A site with only a handful of brief posts gives a reviewer very little to assess.
edits.reason: Removed invented 20-30 article threshold and "rejection rate" claim

edits.find: Each core article should ideally contain 1,000 to 1,500 words of structured analysis. Content must avoid superficial definitions
edits.replace: There is no official word count; length should follow what the topic needs. Content should avoid superficial definitions
edits.reason: Removed invented word-count requirement

edits.find: Top 10 Highest CPC Niches for Google AdSense & Blogging (Up to $50/Click), helps build concentrated topical authority that search engines and advertising evaluators recognize.
edits.replace: Top 10 Highest CPC Niches for Google AdSense & Blogging, helps you build a focused body of useful content.
edits.reason: Removed "$50/Click" hype from anchor; removed unsupported claim about evaluators

edits.find: Google's search systems and ad compliance algorithms actively identify content produced purely for ranking manipulation. While artificial intelligence can assist in outlining and research workflows—as explored in our evaluation of the Top 7 Best AI SEO Tools to Rank Higher on Google (Tested & Compared)—publishing raw, unedited AI output without proprietary data, personal insight, or human editorial refinement directly breaches the Google Search Essentials.
edits.replace: Google Search Central states that appropriate use of AI or automation is not against its guidelines, but using automation, including AI, to generate content with the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings violates its spam policies (see Google Search Essentials). AI can help with outlining and research, as discussed in our overview of AI SEO tools, but unedited AI output adds little that readers can't already find.
edits.reason: Corrected misstatement of Google AI-content guidance with verified source; removed "Tested" anchor claim

edits.find: If your primary menu features four topical categories, each category archive must contain at least 4 to 6 live, fully published articles. Reviewers immediately reject sites featuring "Lorem Ipsum" text, broken internal links, or navigation items leading to 404 errors.
edits.replace: Every category linked from your menu should contain real, published articles. Placeholder ("Lorem Ipsum") text, broken internal links, and menu items leading to 404 errors make a site look unfinished.
edits.reason: Removed invented 4-6 article per category rule and "immediately reject" claim

edits.find: Server instability during the 1-to-14 day AdSense evaluation window can trigger the dreaded "Site down or unavailable" rejection. Your hosting infrastructure must deliver consistent uptime and low Time to First Byte (TTFB). Evaluating performance benchmarks—such as those detailed in our comparison of the Best Web Hosting for WordPress (Speed Tests, TTFB & Pricing Compared)—ensures that automated review crawlers never encounter timeouts or DNS connection failures.
edits.replace: Server instability during the review, which Google says usually takes a few days but can take 2–4 weeks, can lead to a "Site down or unavailable" notice. Your hosting should deliver consistent uptime and reasonable response times. Our comparison of WordPress hosting: speed, TTFB, and pricing covers what to look for, which helps reduce the risk of timeouts or DNS failures while your site is being checked.
edits.reason: Corrected review window to Google-stated timing; removed "ensures never" overclaim; updated anchor

edits.find: With mobile traffic accounting for well over half of global web page visits, Google reviews properties on a mobile-first basis. Your theme must feature
edits.replace: Google Search uses the mobile version of a site's content for indexing and ranking, and many of your readers will see your pages on phones. Your theme should feature
edits.reason: Replaced unsourced mobile-traffic stat and unverified AdSense mobile-first claim with sourced Search fact

edits.find: Intrusive popups, aggressive modal overlays, and full-screen script blockers will result in immediate disqualification.
edits.replace: Intrusive popups, aggressive modal overlays, and full-screen script blockers create a poor experience and are best removed before you apply.
edits.reason: Removed unverified "immediate disqualification" claim

edits.find: Sites with modest, organic traffic can and do receive approval daily.
edits.replace: Sites with modest organic traffic can be approved.
edits.reason: Removed unverifiable "daily" claim

edits.find: However, applying with zero visitors presents practical hurdles. Review algorithms analyze behavioral engagement indicators—such as crawl frequency and organic indexing—to confirm the legitimacy of your domain. A healthy baseline to establish prior to submission is approximately 50 to 100 organic search impressions and consistent daily visitors recorded in Google Search Console.
edits.replace: That said, Google's eligibility page says your content should be able to attract an audience. It is sensible to confirm that your main pages are indexed and starting to appear in Google Search Console before applying, but there is no published visitor or impression minimum.
edits.reason: Removed invented 50-100 impression baseline and claims about review algorithms

While developing sustainable organic search distribution, publishers can also explore broader monetization models summarized in our guide to the Top 5 Realistic Ways to Earn Money Online (Zero Fluff Guide).
edits.replace: puts your site at odds with the AdSense Program Policies, which prohibit paid-to-click programs and third-party services that generate clicks or impressions. Violations can lead to ad serving being limited or an account being disabled. edits.replace: Your own domain that you control (e.g., .com, .org, .net, or a country-code domain)
edits.reason: Clarified wording

edits.replace: Privacy Policy with Google's required disclosures; About Us, Contact, and Terms recommended
edits.reason: Distinguished required vs recommended pages

edits.find: 25 to 35+ original, comprehensive articles (1,000+ words each)
edits.replace: Enough original, substantial articles to show real value (Google sets no minimum)
edits.reason: Removed invented article/word-count thresholds

edits.find: At least 3-4 established categories with 5+ articles each
edits.replace: No empty or placeholder categories; each section has real articles
edits.reason: Removed invented category thresholds

edits.find: SSL active (HTTPS), TTFB under 600ms, passes mobile test
edits.replace: HTTPS active, fast and reliable server responses, mobile-friendly layout
edits.reason: Removed arbitrary TTFB threshold presented as a requirement

edits.find: • Request Review and Wait: Return to the AdSense console, confirm that the code snippet is in place, and submit your site. The standard review timeframe typically spans between 48 hours and two weeks. Do not remove the verification snippet or drastically alter site navigation while the evaluation is underway.
edits.replace: • Request Review and Wait: Return to the AdSense console, confirm that the code snippet is in place, and submit your site. Google says the review "usually takes a few days, but in some cases can take 2-4 weeks," and warns that removing and resubmitting your site can delay the process (Check the status of your AdSense sites). Keep the code in place and avoid major navigation changes while the review is underway.
edits.reason: Corrected review timeframe to Google-stated figure with source

edits.find: This is the most common rejection reason. It indicates that your content either lacks depth, repeats information readily available elsewhere, or consists of thin articles. To remediate this issue, audit your post catalog: remove or consolidate thin articles under 600 words, eliminate generic regurgitated summaries, add primary data, case studies, or actionable tutorials, and expand your catalog to 30+ authoritative articles before reapplying.
edits.replace: This notice indicates that Google did not find enough valuable content: pages may lack depth, repeat information readily available elsewhere, or be thin. To address it, audit your posts: improve, merge, or remove thin articles, cut generic summaries, add genuinely useful explanations and tutorials, and fix navigation before you request another review.
edits.reason: Removed unverified "most common" claim and invented 600-word / 30-article thresholds

edits.find: Google permits only one active AdSense account per individual or registered business entity. If you previously created an AdSense account using an old email address, Google's identity verification system will associate your tax details, phone number, or payee address with the duplicate record. You must either sign in to the original account and add the new domain or formally close the old account before proceeding.
edits.replace: Google states that AdSense policies only allow one AdSense account per publisher. Duplicates are usually identified by matching details such as payee name, address, or phone number. Use your existing account (you can add new sites to it), or close the duplicate account as Google's help page describes.
edits.reason: Sourced one-account rule from Google help

edits.find: Earning AdSense authorization is a significant milestone, but maintaining good standing requires ongoing vigilance. New publisher accounts are placed under elevated monitoring for invalid traffic (IVT) and ad placement compliance during their initial 90 days of operation.
edits.replace: Earning AdSense approval is a milestone, but keeping an account in good standing requires ongoing compliance with the program policies, especially around invalid traffic (IVT) and ad placement.
edits.reason: Removed unverified "90-day elevated monitoring" claim

edits.find:
• Never Click Your Own Ads: Even a single accidental click on your own live advertisements can trigger automated account flags. If you need to test site layout or ad formatting, use publisher development mode or browser extension ad blockers during local editing.
  • Maintain Healthy Ad Density: Google requires that content noticeably outweighs advertising real estate.
edits.replace:
• Never Click Your Own Ads: The AdSense Program Policies state that clicking your own ads for any reason is prohibited. When checking your layout, avoid interacting with live ads.
  • Maintain Healthy Ad Density: Google's publisher policies do not allow Google-served ads on screens with more ads or paid promotional material than publisher content.
edits.reason: Sourced own-click and ad-density policies; removed non-existent "publisher development mode"

edits.find: According to official Google support documentation, most reviews are completed within 48 to 72 hours. However, in instances where manual site evaluation is required or domain traffic verification is pending, the review window can extend from one to four weeks. Publishers should monitor their AdSense dashboard and ensure the verification code remains untouched throughout this period.
edits.replace: Google's help pages say the review "usually takes a few days, but in some cases can take 2-4 weeks" (Google AdSense Help). Keep the AdSense code in place and don't remove and resubmit your site, which Google says can delay the process.
edits.reason: FAQ misquoted Google (48-72 hours); replaced with exact official wording

edits.find: Yes. Domain age itself is not an official eligibility barrier outside specific regional requirements (such as certain international markets where 6-month domain ownership was historically recommended). Provided your new website satisfies technical speed, navigational clarity, mandatory legal pages, and high-value original content requirements, a young domain can earn full approval.
edits.replace: Domain age is not listed in Google's AdSense eligibility requirements. A new site that has original, valuable content, works reliably, and follows the program policies can be approved, although approval is never guaranteed.
edits.reason: Removed unverified regional 6-month rule

edits.find: Google has clarified in its search guidelines that it does not penalize AI-assisted content merely because it was generated with algorithmic tools. Rather, Google evaluates content quality, factual reliability, and user value. However, unedited, bulk-generated programmatic copy that lacks original perspective or human verification will be categorized as low-value inventory and rejected.
edits.replace: Google Search Central has said that appropriate use of AI or automation is not against its guidelines; what matters is quality and usefulness. Unedited, bulk-generated copy that lacks original perspective or human fact-checking is, however, likely to be judged low value.
edits.reason: Added source; softened absolute claim

edits.find: Take at least two to four weeks to conduct a thorough content overhaul: delete or rewrite substandard posts, publish 10 to 15 fresh comprehensive articles, expand author bios,
edits.replace: Use the time to conduct a thorough content overhaul: delete or rewrite substandard posts, add genuinely useful new articles, make author information accurate and complete,
edits.reason: Removed arbitrary time and article-count prescriptions
